title: CSS fundamentals
goal: Apply a small, predictable set of styles.
explanation: CSS rules combine selectors with declarations. A class selector such as .card targets elements with that class. Separate structure from presentation so one rule can style many elements.

The cascade decides which declaration wins. Origin, importance, layers, specificity and order all matter; within otherwise equal rules, a later declaration wins. Avoid solving every conflict with !important.
Some properties, such as colour, are inherited. Others, such as margins, are not normally inherited. Use the browser Styles and Computed panels to see the winning value.
exercise: Style three cards with a shared class, then inspect the computed heading size.
hint: Give each card class="card" and write one shared rule.

quiz.question: Which selector targets class="card"?
quiz.explanation: A dot selects a class. A hash selects an id.
